extra.message: The 'copyline' query parameter from request.GET is concatenated directly into an HTML string (line 32) and returned with content_type='text/html' without any escaping. extra.message: course_preflet_roll_065 parses the JSON request body and blindly merges it into the workset dict via workset.update(change_set). The default workset contains security-relevant attributes ('role', 'is_admin', 'credit_limit') that any client can override arbitrarily (e.g. {"is_admin": true}), an improperly controlled modification of dynamically-determined object attributes that bypasses the intended authorization defaults.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: course_roster_fold_066 returns a hardcoded live partner sync token ('tok_live_partner_sync') and a tax reference/SSN ('739-44-1982') in its JSON response. Secrets and PII are embedded in source code and disclosed to any caller who holds the shared internal ops token.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: course_delta_134 lets the client control the ledger 'state': ledger["state"] is assigned directly from payload['state']/request.GET['state'] (default 'approved'), so a client can force approval state regardless of the computed balance/limit rule. The unvalidated 'amount' (default -250) similarly flips the balance past the limit while state remains approved — a business-logic/trust-boundary flaw.

cwe: CWE-840: Business Logic Errors
CWE-20: Improper Input Validation

extra.message: The 'lane' parameter from request.GET/request.POST is passed to Django's redirect() without any validation or host allowlist. This is an open redirect on /ops/after/course-lane-162/ — an attacker can redirect users to an arbitrary absolute URL (e.g. phishing pages).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: course_wire_tally_222 logs the entire decoded request body and the Authorization bearer token at WARNING level (logger.warning("ops tally body=%s bearer=%s", ...)). Credentials and sensitive payloads are persisted to log files, exposing them to anyone with access to logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The 'ref' query parameter is interpolated into a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") with no sanitization, then written with target.write_text(). A value such as '../../...' escapes the export directory and allows arbitrary file writes (with .json suffix) anywhere the process has permissions; the written content also stores SSN ('ssn' param) and card number ('card' param) in plaintext.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: course_digest_fold_283 hashes the client-supplied 'phrase' with hashlib.md5(). MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash and must not be used for security purposes (passwords, tokens, integrity); a modern algorithm (SHA-256+) or a password KDF (PBKDF2/bcrypt/scrypt) should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-328: Use of Weak Hash

extra.message: course_identity_ping_341 is routed at /ops/identity/course-ping-341/ but, unlike every other ops endpoint in this module, performs no _wrk_gate() internal-token check and no authentication/authorization of any kind. Any unauthenticated client can submit identity 'handle'/'channel' data to this internal operations endpoint.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: course_identity_hint_554 authenticates clients by comparing the supplied 'verifier' against hardcoded 4-digit PINs ({"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}) embedded in source (checked at lines 104-107). Hardcoded credentials are recoverable from source/deployed bytecode and 4-digit values are trivially brute-forceable, defeating the verifier check.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password

extra.message: course_origin_mirror_564 reflects the client-controlled Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any origin can therefore make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the responses, allowing theft of authenticated data from victims' browsers.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CWE-346: Origin Validation Error

extra.message: course_frame_slip_574 actively disables browser security protections by setting X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy on its response, intentionally weakening the application's default defense-in-depth posture (protection mechanism failure / security misconfiguration).

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The 'fragment' query parameter (line 131) is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered: Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). The template is not sandboxed, so this is server-side template injection leading to remote code execution — e.g. fragment={{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} can be used to reach and invoke arbitrary Python objects.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The 'name' query parameter is used directly as a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) and the raw request body is written to it via target.write_bytes(request.body). A name containing '../' sequences (or an absolute path) escapes the export directory, enabling arbitrary file write/upload of arbitrary content anywhere the process has permissions.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: course_nonce_roll_604 generates security-relevant codes/nonces with the non-cryptographic random module (random.choice). Values produced by random are predictable; the secrets module must be used for tokens/codes. cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)
CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: course_xml_fold_616 parses the untrusted XML request body with lxml using etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entities are resolved and network access is enabled, enabling XXE attacks: local file disclosure via file:// entities, SSRF via http:// SYSTEM identifiers, and entity-expansion (billion laughs) denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
CWE-776: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs

extra.message: course_badge_gate_624 grants an elevated access lane ('payroll': 'full', 'casework': 'open') based solely on the client-controlled ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header equaling the string 'lead'. Relying on a cookie/header value without any validation, integrity check, or server-side authentication allows trivial privilege escalation by any client who sets the cookie.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
CWE-287: Improper Authentication
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The 'host' query parameter from request.GET is concatenated directly into an os.system() shell command: _os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). Shell metacharacters (;, &&, ||, $(...), backticks) in the host value allow arbitrary OS command injection with the web server's privileges. Use subprocess.run with a list argv and shell=False, or validate the host against a strict allowlist.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: course_trust_drift_644 creates an SSL context with ssl._create_unverified_context() and passes it to urllib.request.urlopen(), disabling certificate/hostname verification for the outbound HTTPS request. This accepts any certificate and exposes the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'local-dev-insecure-change-me' when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If the application is deployed without the variable, anyone knowing this public default can forge session cookies, password-reset tokens, and CSRF tokens, compromising all users.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: DEBUG defaults to True via env_bool("DJANGO_DEBUG", True). If the environment variable is unset in production, Django serves detailed debug pages on errors, disclosing stack traces, settings values, and environment data to attackers.

cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: get_client_ip returns the first entry of the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header whenever it is present, and this value is stored as AuditLog.ip_address. Without a trusted-proxy allowlist, any request can forge the IP recorded in the security audit trail, undermining audit-log integrity.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: The CSV export (admin_exports) writes user-controlled fields — assignment titles, course codes, usernames, emails — into CSV cells via csv.DictWriter without neutralizing spreadsheet formula characters (=, +, -, @). A malicious instructor-controlled assignment title such as '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '=cmd|...' executes as a formula when the exported grades/submissions CSV is opened in Excel/LibreOffice (CSV/formula injection against the school admin).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
